newsitem.title: JAPAN: New Japan Bullet train matches French world record.
newsitem.headline: New Japan Bullet train matches French world record.

text.p: A new Japanese "Bullet Train" which began regular runs on Saturday matched the French world record for top speed by commercial trains, a spokesman for West Japan Railway Co (JR West) said.

The new 500-series "Nozomi" (Hope) train achieved a top speed of 300 kph (187 mph) during its inaugural service between western Japan's Osaka and Hakata on the southwestern main island of Kyushu, a spokesman for said.

According to the Guinness Book of World Records 1997, the France's TGV train runs at a top speed of 186 mph (297.6 kph), but the JR West spokesman said the correct top commercial speed for the TGV was 300 kph (187 mph).
"In any case, we have only matched the TGV's top speed," the spokesman said.
But JR West would still apply for the Guinness record for the fastest average speed between two regular stops.

Nozomi 500 covers Hiroshima and Kokura, a distance of 192 km (120 miles) in 44 minutes for an average speed of 261.8 kph (163.6 mph), which is faster than TGV's top average 157-mph (252.1-kph) run between Paris and St. Pierre de Corps.
Hiroshima and Kokura are stops between the train's two end stations, Osaka and Hakata.
JR West also said it will ask Guinness to create a new item for fastest average speed from start to finish.
Nozomi's average 252.5 kph (151.5 mph) for the complete Osaka-Hakata run will be the fastest average speed for a train's entire service, the JR West spokesman said.

The tapered Nozomi 500 is scheduled to make two roundtrips a day during holiday seasons and one a day in other times. The service may be extended further east to Tokyo in the fall, the JR West spokesman said.
